test_title: PYST 42: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 30 Oct, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We were asked to vote for the candidates by __raising our hands to indicate voting for or against a proposition__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **a show of hands**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"a show of hands"** means a method of voting or expressing an opinion in a group, where people raise their hands to indicate their choice. (हाथ उठाकर मतदान करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The committee decided to vote on the proposal through a show of hands.
 
 
 
• The phrase is commonly used in meetings or gatherings to quickly determine the majority opinion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **a show of hands**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Changing hands** (हाथ बदलना): Refers to something being passed from one person to another, typically ownership or possession.

 
 
• **Example:** The antique vase has been changing hands among collectors for decades.
 
 
 
• **Tipping our hands** (अपना इरादा प्रकट करना): Means revealing one's intentions or plans unintentionally.
 
 
• **Example:** He tipped his hand during the meeting, revealing his true motives.
 
 
 
• **Getting out of hand** (नियंत्रण से बाहर हो जाना): Refers to a situation becoming chaotic or uncontrollable.
 
 
• **Example:** The party got out of hand when uninvited guests showed up.
